newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end firmer, eye on U.S. ECI data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end firmer, eye on U.S. ECI data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in very quiet trade on Monday, taking direction from U.S. treasuries, with dealers in both countries focusing on Tuesday's U.S. employment cost data.

"It's very dead. It's like everybody stayed at the cottage," said Hank Cunningham, director of fixed income with First Marathon Securities Ltd. "Everyone is also poised, waiting for the ECI tomorrow."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.37 to C$120.45 to yield 6.446 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 21/32 to yield 6.41 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to four basis points from one at Friday's close.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets traded on very thin volumes ahead of the release of the U.S. employment cost index for the second quarter on Tuesday. The report is known to be closely watched by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan and should offer clues about the next move in interest rates.
U.S. treasuries rose on volumes described as anemic and techical factors dominated trading.

In Canada, the long end remains the best performing part of the yield curve. Dealers said speculation that weakness in the dollar would prompt the Bank of Canada to hike interest rates weighed in the short end in recent sessions.
"It's be long or be wrong in this market. If you're not 10 years or longer, you're losing out," said Cunningham.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.24 to C$109.80 to yield 5.919 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 11/32 to yield 6.13 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 21 basis points from 23 basis points at Friday's close.
